Compass

No compass? Plant a stick, mark the shadow tip, wait 15 minutes, mark again. The first mark is west, the second east.

MESSAGES
LONGER RANGE

📡 Meshtastic radios Coming

Small LoRa radios (about 30–40 €) pair with your phone over Bluetooth and pass messages and positions from radio to radio for kilometres, with no network or satellite. Next step for Tent Mate: friends on the map, group chat and alerts in the mountains.

🛰️ Satellite SOS

Some recent phones (for example iPhone 14 and later, Pixel 9 and later) can text emergency services via satellite with no signal. Check in your phone settings whether yours can, and try its demo before you go.

🔐 Your account

Your profile lives only on this phone: no sign-up, no server, works offline. Online sync with Borgo and Barfront will come later and only if you choose it.

EMERGENCY

SOS

Call 112

Text my location to someone

Emergency calls use any network that can reach you, even without your own signal.

112 · 911

112 works across Europe, 911 in the US and Canada. Both often work with no credit and on another carrier's network. In the mountains ask for mountain rescue.

  1. Where you are: coordinates (Map tab), trail, altitude.
  2. What happened and how many people.
  3. Injured: conscious, breathing, bleeding.
  4. Keep your phone on and the line free.

Get found

Alpine distress signal: 6 signals a minute, a minute's pause, repeat. Reply: 3 a minute.

  • Helicopter: both arms up in a Y = "yes, we need help". One arm up, one down = "no".
  • Three fires, three whistles or three of anything mean distress.

Before you go

Most rescues start because nobody knew where you went. Tell someone, like AllTrails Lifeline or GeoResQ tracking.

WhatsAppSMS

If you are not back and do not confirm, Tent Mate alerts your contacts by itself with your last position. They only need the link, no app.

The 10 essentials

In Italy: GeoResQ

The free app of the Soccorso Alpino (CNSAS) and CAI: sends your exact position to mountain rescue and tracks your route. Install it before you go, and still call 112.

Taylor's offline brain

Download Gemma 4, Google's open AI model, into your phone once (about 2 GB, use Wi-Fi). Then Taylor recognizes your photos and answers questions with no internet at all.

Needs a recent phone with Chrome (WebGPU) and at least 6–8 GB of RAM. On older phones Taylor uses the guided questions and the offline library.
